papers.title: The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice
papers.abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, fundamentally driven by the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm, rely on setting external objectives and iterative trial-and-error. When confronted with complex nonlinear problems containing noise and conflicting constraints, this paradigm inherently induces statistical smoothing and compromise, yielding black-box models that lack interpretability and out-of-distribution generalization. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology, reconstructing the solving process into four irreversible stages: Deconstruction, Structure, Construction, and Solving. The method suspends a priori presuppositions to strip unit coupling, extracts rigid invariants inherent to the problem, constructs equivalent mappings anchored to these invariants, and executes the mapping directly to generate the solution. Evaluation metrics and experience are relegated to a posteriori verification. Demonstrated through cross-disciplinary practices including number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, this methodology transcends the statistical fitting bottleneck. Structure-Driven and Objective-Driven methodologies are complementary: when structure is sufficient, solutions are directly constructed; when lacking, it degenerates into the OD path.

papers.title: Further Generalization of Ramanujan Sums with Regular A-Functions
papers.abstract: In the study of Ramanujan sums, the so-called regular $A$-function is a set-valued multiplicative function that tracks certain subsets of the divisor sets of natural numbers. McCarthy provided a generalization of the Ramanujan sum using these regular $A$-function based arithmetic convolutions. This approach has recently attracted considerable interest from several researchers. In this paper, we extend McCarthy's generalization by introducing two regular $A$-functions corresponding to both parameters in the Ramanujan sum. Our generalization exhibits several properties of the Ramanujan sums. Using the regular $A$-function, We also generalize the greatest common divisor (GCD) function and the Von Sterneck formula. Our introduction of two regular $A$-functions into these expressions enables us to explore a novel perspective on the connection between these expressions and the order relation between the two regular $A$-functions. In particular, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for orthogonality and Dedekind-H\"older's identity (i.e., Ramanujan sum = Von Sterneck function) to hold. Our primary motivation for the proposed generalization is Ramanujan expansions of arithmetic functions based on arbitrary regular $A$-functions. These expansions of arbitrary $A$-functions discussed here are new in the literature.

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
papers.abstract: A finite nonempty subset of the positive integers is first-order Schreier if the minimum element of that set is greater than or equal to the size of the set. A nonempty subset of the positive integers $X$ is second-order Schreier if $X$ is a union of $d$ first-order Schreier sets for some $d \leq \min X$. We study a combinatorial relationship between the count of second-order Schreier sets and the Fibonacci sequence. Specifically, we show that the second-order Schreier set with minimum $2$ and maximum $n+4$ is one more than the $n^{\text{th}}$ term of the convolution of the Fibonacci numbers $(F_1, F_2, \ldots)$ with $(F_2, F_3, \ldots)$ (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).
